questions.q: What happens to a resource once public access is disabled on its Networking tab?
options: It can no longer be reached by IP address or URL from outside Azure's private network
It becomes permanently unreachable, even from inside the VNet
It automatically deletes itself for security reasons
Nothing changes until the resource is also deleted and recreated
questions.explain: Disabling public access removes reachability from outside Azure's private network — a private endpoint is then needed for legitimate access.

questions.q: Why isn't disabling public access alone enough for a working setup?
options: It would also cut off legitimate traffic from your own application, not just attackers
Public access can't actually be disabled on any Azure service
It only works for storage accounts, not AI services
It requires a separate Azure subscription to take effect
questions.explain: Disabling public access blocks everyone, including your own app — a private endpoint is needed to restore legitimate access privately.

questions.q: What does a private endpoint actually provide?
options: A discount on the resource's pricing tier
Its own network interface inside your VNet, with a private IP address reachable only from that network
A public IP address with extra firewall rules
Automatic encryption of data at rest
questions.explain: A private endpoint is a NIC inside your own virtual network, with a private IP — reachable only from inside that VNet or a connected network.

questions.q: What has to happen before a private endpoint connection actually passes traffic?
options: The connection must be approved on the resource it's connecting to
Nothing — traffic flows immediately once the endpoint is created
The resource must be moved to a different Azure region
Public access must be re-enabled
questions.explain: A private endpoint connection sits pending until it's approved on the target resource — one more checkpoint before traffic flows.

questions.q: What changes in your application's SDK calls or authentication when you move from a public endpoint to a private one?
options: Nothing — the API, SDK calls, and authentication all stay identical; only the network path changes
The authentication method must switch from keys to certificates
Every SDK call must be rewritten to use a new private API
The application must be rebuilt as a container
questions.explain: A private endpoint changes the network path only — there's no public IP left to find, but the API surface and auth are unchanged.
